_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present -er
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -er verbs.
entries.example: Je parle français.

entries.label: Present -ir/-re
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -ir and -re verbs.
entries.example: Je finis, tu vends.

entries.label: Passé composé (avoir)
entries.usage: A finished past with avoir.
entries.example: J'ai mangé une pomme.

entries.label: Passé composé (être)
entries.usage: Past with être — motion and reflexives.
entries.example: Elle est partie tôt.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: Je jouais souvent.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: Demain je partirai.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: What would happen.
entries.example: Je voudrais partir.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: After que — wish, doubt, necessity.
entries.example: Il faut que tu viennes.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Parle plus fort !

entries.label: Pluperfect
entries.usage: The past-before-the-past.
entries.example: J'avais déjà mangé.

entries.label: Être (to be)
entries.usage: Saying what someone or something is.
entries.example: Je suis étudiant. — I am a student.

entries.label: Avoir (to have)
entries.usage: Saying what you have — and how old, hungry or thirsty you are.
entries.example: J'ai vingt ans. — I am twenty years old.

entries.point: Key irregular presents (vais, fais, peux, veux)
entries.label: Present irregulars
entries.usage: Now or regularly, for the everyday verbs that break the pattern.
entries.example: Je vais au marché maintenant. — I'm going to the market now.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: Saying that something is not so.
entries.example: Je ne parle pas anglais. — I don't speak English.

entries.point: Il y a — there is / there are
entries.label: Il y a
entries.usage: Saying what exists or is present, one thing or many.
entries.example: Il y a un livre sur la table. — There is a book on the table.

entries.label: Reflexives
entries.usage: When you do something to yourself — washing, waking, getting up.
entries.example: Chaque matin, je me lève à sept heures. — Every morning I get up at seven.

entries.point: Near future & recent past (aller / venir de)
entries.label: Near future/past
entries.usage: About to happen, or only just finished.
entries.example: Attends, je vais arriver dans cinq minutes. — Wait, I'm going to arrive in five minutes.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: Telling someone what another person said or asked.
entries.example: Il dit qu'il est fatigué. — He says (that) he is tired.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: When the thing acted on comes first and who did it barely matters.
entries.example: La lettre est écrite en français. — The letter is written in French.

entries.label: Si clauses
entries.usage: Imagining something that is not true right now.
entries.example: Si j'étais riche, je voyagerais partout. — If I were rich, I would travel everywhere.

entries.label: Gérondif
entries.usage: Doing one thing while, or by, doing another.
entries.example: Il est tombé en courant après le bus. — He fell while running for the bus.

entries.label: Subjunctive (bien que, pour que)
entries.usage: After linking words like bien que and pour que.
entries.example: Bien qu'il fasse froid, ils se baignent. — Although it's cold, they swim.

entries.label: Past conditional
entries.usage: What would have happened, but did not.
entries.example: Si j'avais su, je serais venu plus tôt. — If I had known, I would have come earlier.

entries.point: The past subjunctive & sequence of tenses
entries.label: Past subjunctive
entries.usage: After que, for something already over and done.
entries.example: Je suis ravi que tu sois venu. — I'm delighted that you came.

entries.label: Passé simple
entries.usage: The written past of novels and history — read, not spoken.
entries.example: Le roi construisit un grand palais. — The king built a great palace.

entries.label: Elevated register
entries.usage: Formal and literary French that everyday speech has dropped.
entries.example: Je crains qu'il ne vienne trop tard. — I fear he will come too late.

entries.label: Definite article
entries.usage: le/la/les.
entries.example: le livre, la porte

entries.label: Indefinite article
entries.usage: un/une/des.
entries.example: un chat, des chats

entries.label: Partitive
entries.usage: some / any of something.
entries.example: du pain, de la eau

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender and number.
entries.example: une voiture bleue

entries.label: Possessive/demonstrative
entries.usage: mon/ma/mes, ce/cette/ces.
entries.example: mon ami, cette nuit

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: The words for I, you, he and we — with tu or vous for you.
entries.example: Je suis de Paris. — I am from Paris.

entries.label: Noun gender/plural
entries.usage: Every thing counts as a he or a she, and the plural is written but barely heard.
entries.example: J'ai deux livres. — I have two books.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: Asking where, how, when, why and how much.
entries.example: Où habites-tu ? — Where do you live?

entries.label: Direct object pronouns
entries.usage: Saying him, her or them instead of naming the thing again.
entries.example: Tu connais Marc? Oui, je le connais bien. — Do you know Marc? Yes, I know him well.

entries.point: Indirect pronouns, y and en (lui, leur, y, en)
entries.label: Lui, y, en
entries.usage: To him, to them, there, or some of it.
entries.example: Je téléphone à Paul; je lui téléphone ce soir. — I'm calling Paul; I'll call him tonight.

entries.point: Two object pronouns (je le lui donne)
entries.label: Pronoun order
entries.usage: When two short words like le and lui meet before the verb, in a fixed order.
entries.example: Ce livre? Je te le prête volontiers. — This book? I'll gladly lend it to you.

entries.label: Relative pronouns
entries.usage: Adding who, that or where to say more about a person or thing.
entries.example: C'est l'homme qui habite à côté. — That's the man who lives next door.

entries.label: Comparative/superlative
entries.usage: Saying more than, less than, or the most.
entries.example: Paris est plus grand que Lyon. — Paris is bigger than Lyon.

entries.label: Irregular comparatives
entries.usage: Better and worse, which have words of their own.
entries.example: Ce restaurant est meilleur que l'autre. — This restaurant is better than the other.

entries.label: Connectors
entries.usage: Joining ideas: so, however, because, on the other hand.
entries.example: Il pleut, donc nous restons à la maison. — It's raining, so we're staying home.

entries.point: Emphasis (c'est… qui / que, ce qui… c'est)
entries.label: Emphasis
entries.usage: Pushing one word to the front so it stands out.
entries.example: C'est moi qui ai préparé le dîner. — I'm the one who made the dinner.
